## Step 1: Overview of a Write-Ahead Log
A write-ahead log (WAL) is a mechanism used by databases to ensure data consistency and durability in the face of failures. It's essentially a record of all changes made to the database before they're actually written to disk.

## Step 2: How WAL Works
When a database makes changes to its data, it first writes those changes to a log, which is a separate file or set of files. This log contains a record of each operation, including the operation type, the data being modified, and any relevant metadata. Once the changes are safely written to the log, the database then applies those changes to the actual data on disk.

## Step 3: Role of WAL in Recovery
In the event of a crash or failure, the database can use the WAL to recover the state of the data. After startup, the database will replay the log entries from the most recent checkpoint forward, effectively reapplying all changes that were made up to the point of failure. This ensures that the database returns to a consistent state, even if some of the data on disk was damaged or corrupted.
